Rules / Modernization

SK1063 Use the interpolation form that says what it means

A string.Format whose holes are numbered, a ToString() inside an interpolation hole, or a string literal sitting in a hole instead of in the text.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floorC# 6.0
Since1.3

Why

string.Format("{0} of {1}", done, total) makes the reader carry two numbers across a comma to find out what goes where, and the compiler will not tell them when the arguments are swapped. The interpolated form puts the value where it is printed. The two smaller shapes are the same argument applied to interpolation itself: $"{count.ToString()}" renders through a string nobody keeps, and $"a{"b"}c" is a hole holding something that was never a variable.

Example

Instead of:

var line = string.Format("{0} of {1}", done, total);
var label = $"{count.ToString()} left";
var path = $"{root}{"/"}{name}";

Write:

var line = $"{done} of {total}";
var label = $"{count} left";
var path = $"{root}/{name}";

When it does not fire

⚠ `SK2016` reports the one place interpolation must not be used, and this rule must not create that finding: a string.Format whose result is handed to a Microsoft.Extensions.Logging message parameter is left alone, because rewriting it would eagerly render the message the logger was going to render lazily. ⚠ Overload resolution is the trap that makes the rewrite unsound where it bites. An interpolated string converts to string, to FormattableString and to IFormattable, so a call site with a FormattableString overload beside the string one — EF Core's FromSql family is the well-known case — can bind somewhere else after the rewrite, and there the difference is whether the SQL is parameterised. The rule reads the member group at the call site and declines if any candidate takes FormattableString or IFormattable in that position. ⚠ The placeholders must be `{0}`…`{n-1}`, each used exactly once and in ascending order. A repeated index would evaluate its argument twice; an out-of-order one would evaluate the arguments in a different order; a gap means an argument is unused. Every argument must be a chain of plain names, so nothing with a comma or a colon in it lands inside a hole, where both are grammar. The IFormatProvider overloads are refused outright — the culture is the point of them — as are a non-literal or verbatim format string and an explicitly passed object[]. ⚠ `x.ToString()` inside a hole is removable only for a value type. On a reference type null.ToString() throws where $"{null}" renders empty, which is not a modernization but a behaviour change; Nullable<T> is admitted because both spellings render the empty string. A hole carrying a format clause is left alone. ⚠ Not covered, deliberately: NestedStringInterpolation, PassStringInterpolation, and UseFormatSpecifierInFormatString — the last because x.ToString("N2") and $"{x:N2}" agree only where the instance method delegates to IFormattable, which the BCL numeric types do and a user type need not.
